summary.title: From Source Code To Machine Code: Build Your Own Compiler From Scratch
summary.one_liner: You learn how programming languages work by building a minimal interpreter, a bytecode compiler, and finally a compiler that emits x64 ELF executables for a statically typed language.
takeaways: Build a simple calculator interpreter, then add variables, scopes, control flow, and functions.
Design a virtual machine and bytecode, and write a compiler that targets it.
Learn the basics of x64 assembly and how instructions are encoded in bytes.
Translate bytecode into x64 machine code and generate ELF binary executables.
summary.summary: This is an online book that walks through a minimal but complete compiler implementation for a statically typed language, compiling it into x64 ELF executables. It is organized in three parts: an interpreter (calculator, variables and scopes, control flow and functions), a bytecode compiler (virtual machine, variables and expressions, control flow, functions and non-local variables), and machine code (x64 assembly crash course, instruction encoding, translating from virtual machine to real machine, binary executables, pointers and memory). The page lists the contents and notes that a PDF/EPUB and paperback edition are available for purchase; the excerpt itself does not describe the implementation language or detailed code.
